text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
----SERBIA----
POLITIKA
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic says ruling Democratic Party of Socialists has rejected the policies of Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
- Serbian Orthodox Church Synod meets in Dalj, Eastern Slavonia, Croatia; urges local Serbs to stay and preserve their status as a people.
- Serbian state TV earns 410 million dinars (USD 85M) from viewing licences in 1996.
- Bank credits too expensive for most firms - monthly interest rates range from 3.25 pct to over 20 pct.
- Serbian government to present amended version of draft information law soon.
NASA BORBA

- Montenegrin president supports possible candidacy of Slobodan Milosevic for president of the Yugoslav federation; in Montenegrin dispute, faction headed by Prime Minister Djukanovic and Parliament Speaker Svetozar Marovic says they will not give up so easily.
- First reactions to privatization bill: experts say privatization process too slow and law effectively places firms under state control.
- Serbian opposition Zajedno ("Together") coalition presents economic programme, calling for Yugoslavia's membership in the EU by 2005.
- Milosevic, Bulatovic orchestrated coup against me, says Montenegrin opposition leader Novak Kilibarda.
- Serbian private sector to stage protest outside Yugoslav parliament after talks with authorities break down.
- Two Kosovo Albanians shot dead in road ambush.
- Yugoslav authorities bar Bosnian delegates on their way to refugee forum in Belgrade.
- Pope Paul still intends to visit Belgrade, but not before the elections this year.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- European Union donates around 5.6 million German marks of medical equipment to Bosnian Serb Republic.

- The Serbian government has adopted measures for economic and financial consolidation of the construction industry, giving support and priority to the branch as an exporter, said Serbian construction minister Branislav Ivkovic.
BORBA

- Serbian power company Elektroprivreda Srbije plans to invest $420 million this year, and $2.6 billion by the year 2000 in overhaul and building of new facilities. Possibilities exist for employing local companies on development projects.
----MONTENEGRO----
POBJEDA
- Certain statements made by some officials have damaged the reputation of Montenegro and the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists, the party said in a statement.
- President Bulatovic rules out introduction of Montenegrin currency.
- Montenegro's strategic development options lie in tourism and agriculture, Prime Minister Djukanovic said at Food Fair in Budva.
- Delegations of Herceg Novi and Dubrovnik, Croatia, meet to discuss water supply from Dubrovnik for Herceg Novi.
- Teachers, health sector threaten strike over back pay.
- Radio Cetinje journalists on strike over unpaid wages. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 2224254
